title: What "Dungeonpunk" means in Wayfinder
context: Dungeonpunk usually means dungeon-crawling inside an industrial or post-industrial fantasy world, where delving is a job and the dungeons are often built things. Act 1's dungeon is already a sewer under a refinery district.
recommended: Dungeons are made by industry: sewers, refinery works, flooded pump-halls, Compact-licensed ruins, wrecked brume engines. Delving is a trade with brokers, permits, insurers and danger fees, and crews do it for the money.
alternatives: Old-world dungeons (ruins from before the sea went unfixed) explored with gaslit-era gear
Punk as attitude: dungeons are the places the Compact's order doesn't reach, and crews use them to live outside it
A mix: industrial dungeons in the Reach, old-world ruins beyond Kelder's Wall

title: What "Gaslit fantasy" means in Wayfinder
context: Gaslamp fantasy is usually Victorian-era society with magic: gas streetlamps, fog, ledgers, class lines, newspapers. In Wayfinder the lamps already burn charge refined from brume.
recommended: Gaslamp-era society where the 'gas' is refined brume: charge-lamps on every street, refinery smoke, licences and ledgers, top hats and soot, class lines you can see. Magic is an industry and a profession, not a mystery.
alternatives: Gaslit feel only in the cities; the sea and the islands are a frontier age of sail
Gaslit as gothic mood (fog, unseen things, gaslight horror) more than as a technology level
Closer to steampunk: brass machines and sky ships common, not rare

title: How dark is Ashford?
context: Act 1 has three dead sellswords, prejudice at the gate, a girl held by a monster, and a painful binding. Influences you named include One Piece and Indiana Jones.
recommended: Grim streets, hopeful crew. The cruelty is systemic (the Compact, the Bench, how monsterkin and fae are treated) and the danger is real, but the story is about found family, wonder and getting out. Deaths happen off-screen or to strangers in Act 1.
alternatives: Darker: gothic horror at the edges, the Gloam's victims shown, real fear
Lighter: pulp adventure, villains are bad but fun, the sewer is more gross than scary

title: How strange is the Gloam?
context: The script calls it 'something made of dark and teeth' that comes apart into warm grey fog in sunlight.
recommended: Uncanny, not gory: it moves wrong, sounds are muffled near it, the lamps don't light it, and it is never seen clearly until the sun holds it.
alternatives: Body horror: something that was once people
Animal: a huge, real beast that hates light

title: Weather and light in Ashford
context: Places text: Refinery Row is built where the refinery's heat keeps the fog off.
recommended: Fog rolls in off the brume every night and burns off by mid-morning everywhere except Refinery Row, which stays clear and warm. Night streets are pools of amber charge-light in grey.
alternatives: Permanent haze, sunlight is rare (which makes the Grate Chamber's sunbeam special)
Clear sea air; the fog is only out on the water

title: Humour
context: The broker, Tova and Rook already trade dry jokes in the drafted scenes.
recommended: Keep the banter: dry, quick, character-led, never undercutting a serious beat.
alternatives: More comic, closer to One Piece
Less: keep jokes to a line or two per scene

title: What brume is
context: Lore: the sea is covered in brume; it is 'unfixed'; binding puts brume possibility into a person; the refinery burns 'the unfixed sea for fuel'.
recommended: A grey fog of unfixed Possibility lying on the open sea. Breathed in deep water it slowly unwrites things that aren't bound; refined, it becomes charge; bound into a person, it becomes their class and grade.
alternatives: A substance in the water itself, the fog is only its breath
Something nobody understands; the Compact's explanation is propaganda
You'll write it; keep it vague in Act 1

title: What charge is and what it powers
context: Tinker works with 'mechanisms, clockwork, charge'; the merchant has 'charge-lamp money'; the loaners include a charge lamp.
recommended: Refined brume sealed in glass cells. It lights lamps, runs lifts, pumps and engines, and drives Artifice spells. Charge cells are graded like everything else, and a full F-grade cell costs about a day's wage.
alternatives: Charge is rare and expensive: only the rich have charge-lamps, everyone else burns oil
Charge is liquid, piped through cities like gas

title: Sky ships
context: Enkrid's prologue sparks his dream of the sky ship; influences.md puts it as the mid-to-late game reward.
recommended: They exist but almost nobody has seen one: the legends' expedition was rumoured to use the inventor's brume engine to fly. In Act 1 they are a dream and a rumour.
alternatives: The Compact has a few; you see one over Ashford in Act 1
None exist yet; the inventor's watch is a clue to building the first

title: The Compact
context: Lore: the Compact owns the refinery, the licences and most of the captains; licensed binding carries a debt to it; it writes 'Monster' on manifests.
recommended: A chartered trading company that became a government in all but name: refinery, licences, insurance, wardens, debt. Polite, legal and merciless. In Act 1 it is everywhere but never the villain on screen.
alternatives: A league of noble houses that share a charter
A guild of binders that grew into an empire

title: The Bench
context: Lore: 'The Bench owns the charts.' Rook comes from an old Bench family and was raised to copy charts, never draw one.
recommended: The courts and record-keepers of the Reach: charts, deeds, inheritances and contracts. Bench families are old money that holds the maps, and a chart isn't true until the Bench stamps it.
alternatives: A scholars' academy that controls cartography
A religious order of record-keepers

title: The Wrights
context: Enkrid is schooled at a Wright chapel by Brother Ansel; it's the only building in his village with a clock.
recommended: A faith of makers who teach that the world was wrought, and that fixing things is holy. Chapels keep the clocks and the schools. Tinkers are often Wright-raised.
alternatives: A minor sect, not a main religion
The main church of the mainland, rich and political

title: Law on the streets
context: At the gate a guard asks a monsterkin PC for 'surety' to stay overnight.
recommended: Two forces: the city Watch (underpaid, answers to the Bench) and Compact Wardens (well paid, answer to the refinery). The surety bond for monsterkin is Compact policy the Watch enforces.
alternatives: Only Compact Wardens
A city Watch only; the Compact uses hired sellswords

title: Kelder's Wall
context: Lore: the legends sailed 'out past Kelder's Wall, eight years ago'.
recommended: The edge of the charted Reach: a standing bank of brume that never lifts, graded far above anything in the Reach. Ships that go past it rarely come back.
alternatives: A real wall: an ancient sea-wall of stone across the water
A Compact blockade line

title: Why insurers matter
context: Lore: unclassed crew can't sail because insurers won't cover them.
recommended: The Compact underwrites every voyage out of Ashford. No policy, no berth, no harbour will take you. That's the real reason class is a gate.
alternatives: Independent underwriters' houses that compete
No insurers; it's a captain's superstition

title: How fae are treated
context: Lore: 'Fae are closer to unfixed than anyone alive'; Enkrid is a road fae ('Skirl' in the Reach); a mother pulls her child's arm down.
recommended: Distrusted, not hated: people think fae leak Possibility and bring bad luck aboard. Polite avoidance, higher prices, captains who 'have no berths'. Binding hits fae harder (Enkrid collapses).
alternatives: Openly persecuted
Exotic: welcomed as lucky by sailors, distrusted by the Compact

title: How monsterkin are treated
context: Lore: the Compact writes 'Monster' on manifests; one inn on the quay takes them; Tova is paid less than humans.
recommended: Legal second-class: surety bonds, one inn, lower wages, written policy. Plenty of ordinary people are kind one-to-one; the system isn't.
alternatives: Worse: barred from the city after dark
Milder: it's mostly the Compact's paperwork

title: Who lives in Ashford
context: Ashford has 11,000 people. The drafted NPCs are Human, Vulpine, Dwarf and Half-Orc.
recommended: Mostly Founding peoples (humans, dwarves, half-orcs), a big beastkin quarter by the fish market, few fae, and monsterkin only on the quay.
alternatives: Very mixed, a true crossroads port
Mostly humans; everyone else is visibly a visitor

title: Coin names
context: The rules use cp / sp / gp / pp with prices x3 per grade. The broker says questions will cost 'a silver each'.
recommended: Keep cp/sp/gp/pp in the rules and on sheets, with Reach names in the text: copper bits, silver marks, gold crowns, platinum charters.
alternatives: Use the plain D&D names everywhere
Compact scrip as paper money on top of coin

title: Protagonist 2 and 3's names
context: The deck leaves them TBD. The Game lore drafts call them Rook (Corvine) and Tova (Trollblood). The module uses whatever the lore says, so renaming is one edit.
recommended: Keep Rook and Tova as working names until you choose.
alternatives: Rename them now (write the names in the note)
Let the player name them in play

title: The other drafted names
context: Draft by Claude: Odile Sallow (broker), Hollis and Petra Tarrant, Binder Maren Quell, Old Dunmore, Captain Silvan Rourke, Lady Celestine Varenne, Captain Isolde Varr, Elian Marsh, Aurelio Fenn, Brother Ansel, Dov, Old Gnaw, the Gloam.
recommended: Keep them as placeholders; rename any in the note and the module follows.
alternatives: Replace them all before I play (list your names in the note)

title: What Petra saw from her window
context: Script: 'She saw something from her window and went to look. Rich girls do.'
recommended: Grey fog moving against the wind out of the street grates at night, and a light under the street where no one should be. A hook for what the refinery dumps below.
alternatives: A person she knew going down the culvert hatch
Leave it a mystery Petra won't explain

title: What the Gloam is
context: It avoids sunlight and comes apart into warm grey fog that settles in the water when the light holds it.
recommended: Brume run-off from the refinery that pooled in the dark for forty years until it started wanting. Sunlight fixes it and it falls apart. Nobody in Ashford wants that known, which quietly sets up the Compact.
alternatives: A failed, unlicensed binding: something that was a person
An animal of the unfixed sea that came up the outflow
Leave it unexplained in Act 1

title: Did the broker know?
context: Script: Odile 'suspected'. The danger fee is pressed out of her.
recommended: She suspected from the sellswords' silence and Petra's story, and sent the cheapest crew she could find. Not evil, a broker.
alternatives: She knew exactly, and someone paid her to keep it quiet
She had no idea

title: How Hollis Tarrant pays
context: The fee must be 'enough to bind four' minus the loaner bill, topped up by the danger fee.
recommended: He pays in full and in public, so Refinery Row sees he's generous, and asks them never to mention where Petra was found.
alternatives: He haggles and pays short
He pays through the broker, who takes her cut

title: The three dead sellswords
context: Three Coldwater sellswords went in six days before. Their journal says 'Lamps don't scare it. Light does.'
recommended: Give them names in the journal (Draft) and a Coldwater crew mark, so Coldwater can come back later. Their journal is a handout.
alternatives: Keep them nameless
One survived and is still down there

title: The pocket watch's engraving
context: The script leaves this for you: 'Close-up on the engraving (the user to write what it says)'.
recommended: You write it. Until then the flashback and the item show a blank engraving line you fill in once on the item.
alternatives: 'Keep time for what matters'
Coordinates or a date only the inventor understood
A single word in the inventor's own script

title: How the flashback plays at the table
context: The prologue plays when Enkrid takes out the watch on the Exchange steps.
recommended: Read-aloud with a sepia journal page, played as narration with one or two choices for young Enkrid (no dice), then back to the steps.
alternatives: Played as a short scene with young-Enkrid stats
Skippable narration only

title: Who your character is in Act 1
context: The JRPG plan: a fourth traveller in Ashford also trying to earn a class and passage, with an intro by race family.
recommended: Same as the JRPG: you make one custom character, the trio are fixed characters you also run, and your character's intro depends on their race family.
alternatives: You play Enkrid as the main character instead
All four are yours to build

title: Your character's reason to need a ship
context: The broker asks: 'I'm here for a ship' or 'I'm here for work'.
recommended: Leave it to you at character creation: a short 'Why I need a ship' line on the sheet that the journal prompts refer back to.
alternatives: Offer four ready-made reasons (debt, a lost sibling, exile, a map)
No fixed reason; it comes out in play

title: What binding feels and looks like
context: Script: a white hall, brass coils, glass cylinders of warm grey brume; it hurts; fae take in more than they should.
recommended: The brume goes in through the hands and chest; everything goes white and too-sharp for a moment; it leaves a faint grey vein mark (the 'binding mark') that darkens with each grade.
alternatives: No visible mark
A Compact tattoo/brand recording the debt, even when paid in cash

title: The binding fee
context: Must make the money tight: reward + danger fee − loaner bill = exactly four bindings. Default in the module: 50 gp each (200 gp), reward 160 gp, loaner bill 30 gp, danger fee 70 gp.
recommended: 50 gp per F-grade binding, x3 per grade after (150 gp at E), with the numbers above.
alternatives: Cheaper (20 gp each), so the money is about pride more than survival
Dearer (100 gp each), and the danger fee becomes the real climax

title: How much Rourke shows in Act 1
context: Rourke is later revealed as the antagonist (a mid-level grunt of the series villain).
recommended: Charming and reasonable on the quay; one detail that sticks (his crew is armed like mercenaries, not sailors) that pays off on island 3.
alternatives: Visibly cruel already
Barely seen; the noble is the face of the snub

title: How Act 1 ends at the table
context: The demo ends with the Gilded Tern leaving and a title card; the Second Captain opens Act 2.
recommended: The Tern leaves; a last read-aloud; then one line where a scruffy captain on the next berth has been watching them. Title card. My Story asks you to write the end of Act 1.
alternatives: End on the Tern leaving, nothing more
Play the Second Captain's offer as an epilogue

title: How many days Act 1 covers
context: The JRPG uses a calendar; Act 1 is one city chapter.
recommended: Four days: arrive and take the job (day 1), the Undercourses (day 2, the Gloam at noon), paid and bound (day 3), the missed ship (day 4 morning).
alternatives: One long day and a morning
A week, with time for the broker's board between beats

title: Side work in Act 1
context: The JRPG has filler after the commission: the broker's board, rat culls, the training yard, gathering, journal page 1.
recommended: Include the broker's board (a few F-grade jobs as a roll table) and the outer Undercourses rat cull as optional, off by default in the Director.
alternatives: None; keep Act 1 tight
All of the JRPG's filler

title: The legends' journal page 1
context: The JRPG plans a trail of the legends' lost journal pages, page 1 somewhere in Ashford.
recommended: Hide it in Act 1 at the Lantern and Lee (Dunmore kept a page Captain Varr left with a bar tab). You write its text; the module has a blank handout.
alternatives: Leave it for Act 2
In the Undercourses, among the sellswords' things

title: Who's at the table
context: You said you want to play through it and write your story.
recommended: Solo: you run the world as GM and play all four heroes. The Act 1 Director shows the next beat, posts read-aloud and opens the right map, so you rarely need the journals mid-scene.
alternatives: You GM for a group; players take the heroes
Solo with a GM emulator (oracle rolls for yes/no questions)

title: An oracle for solo play
context: Solo players often use a yes/no oracle to answer questions the script doesn't cover.
recommended: Add a small oracle macro: ask a question, pick likely/even/unlikely, get Yes / Yes, and / Yes, but / No, but / No / No, and.
alternatives: No oracle; follow the script
A fuller emulator with random events

title: Read-aloud
context: The lore has full scripts with speakers, stage notes and choices.
recommended: Post read-aloud lines to chat as the speaker (with their portrait), one tap per block, so the chat log becomes the story so far.
alternatives: Read from the journal only
Show the script as a popup for a second screen

title: Dice
context: Foundry rolls dice for you; some players like real dice.
recommended: Foundry dice by default, with an 'enter my own roll' option on every check.
alternatives: Foundry dice only
Always ask for my roll

title: How My Story works
context: The module has a My Story journal: one page per beat with a prompt, plus a session log the module appends to.
recommended: Keep that: a prompt per beat (what your character said, what changed, a line to remember), the Director's 'Write this beat' button, and an automatic session log of what happened.
alternatives: One free page; no prompts
Prompts plus a chat-log export into the journal at the end of each session

title: Where your story goes afterwards
context: You keep the book's lore in the Game lore Word folder in OneDrive.
recommended: Add a 'Copy my story' button that turns My Story into clean text you can paste into Word.
alternatives: Leave it in Foundry
Export straight to a .docx file

title: Maps or theatre of the mind
context: The module ships generated maps for the city, the Exchange, the Undercourses, the Grate Chamber, the Binding House, the inn and the quay.
recommended: Battle maps for the two fights and the Scene; the rest as scene art you can use or ignore.
alternatives: Battle maps for every location
Theatre of the mind only; maps as handouts

title: Zones on a grid
context: Possibilities uses four zones (Engaged, Near, Far, Distant), not squares.
recommended: Track zones on the sheets; the grid is only for placing tokens so the picture reads.
alternatives: Convert zones to squares (Engaged 1, Near 6, Far 12)
Draw zone regions on each map

title: How hard should Act 1 be
context: Unclassed heroes have about 6 HP each. The Gloam's first fight is a scripted loss.
recommended: Fair but tense: Old Gnaw can drop one hero if you're careless; nobody dies in Act 1 unless you turn on the Undertaking setting.
alternatives: Story-light: fights are short
Harsh: death is possible from the first rat

group: Gaps in the rules the system had to fill
title: Raise Guard
context: The JRPG lists Raise Guard as an action; the effect isn't in the imported data.
recommended: 1 action: +2 AC until the start of your next turn.
alternatives: 2 actions: +4 AC
Use the workbook's Combat Reference text (paste it in the note)

group: Gaps in the rules the system had to fill
title: Aid
context: Aid is one of the three things unclassed heroes can do.
recommended: 1 action: an ally within Near gets +2 on their next check this round.
alternatives: Roll a DC 12 check: success +2, critical +4, critical failure −1
Use the workbook's text (note)

group: Gaps in the rules the system had to fill
title: Stabilise
context: The JRPG decision: anyone can Stabilise for 1 action; 'the most valuable action'.
recommended: Automatic for an Engaged ally at 0 HP; they stop Dying and stay at 0 HP.
alternatives: A Medicine check vs DC 12
Automatic, and restores 1 HP

group: Gaps in the rules the system had to fill
title: Recovery checks while Dying
context: Tabletop: three failed recovery checks in one fight kills. The check's DC isn't in the data.
recommended: At the start of each turn: d20 + CON save vs DC 12. Success = stable; three failures = dead (or Defeated with the Undertaking setting off).
alternatives: A flat d20 vs 10
Use the workbook's text (note)

group: Gaps in the rules the system had to fill
title: Possibility points pool
context: Signatures and spells cost points (tier = cost) from a pool; its size isn't imported.
recommended: 3 + Combat EL, refilled on a long rest.
alternatives: Casting modifier + Combat EL
Use the workbook's Spells & Techniques sheet value (note)

group: Gaps in the rules the system had to fill
title: Profession signatures before binding
context: Professions have signatures too (Smith: Sound Repair). Unclassed heroes have professions in full.
recommended: Usable before binding, from the same pool (3 points when unclassed).
alternatives: Not until bound
Free once per Scene

group: Gaps in the rules the system had to fill
title: Scenes: when a Setback hits
context: Scenes run on Resistance, Setbacks and Full/Half/None approaches.
recommended: On a critical failure always, on a failure when the approach says so, and once at the end of every round the clock moves.
alternatives: Only on failures
Only at the end of each round

group: Gaps in the rules the system had to fill
title: Short rests
context: Hit dice exist (hit dice = Combat EL × the class die) but the rest rules aren't imported.
recommended: A short rest (one watch) spends hit dice: roll each, add CON mod. A long rest restores everything.
alternatives: Short rests restore half HP
No short rests in Act 1

group: Gaps in the rules the system had to fill
title: Unarmed and improvised weapons
context: The damage formula needs a weapon die.
recommended: Unarmed d4; improvised d4 with −2 to hit unless your profession uses the tool (a Tinker with a pry bar uses it at d6).
alternatives: Unarmed d4, improvised d6, no penalty

group: Gaps in the rules the system had to fill
title: XP in Act 1
context: XP to next rank = 50 × EL². Unclassed heroes have no class XP to earn.
recommended: Track profession XP from Scenes, and give a milestone at the end of Act 1; class XP starts after binding.
alternatives: Award XP per challenge exactly as the workbook (8 challenges per rank)
No XP in Act 1

title: Visual touchstones
context: The sheets and maps use soot, brass, verdigris and charge-lamp amber.
recommended: Victorian dockside and refinery, wet stone undercity, brass instruments, ledgers and wax seals. Think Dishonored's streets and Arcane's undercity, kept your own.
alternatives: Brighter: sun-bleached port, the gloom only underground
Name your own touchstones in the note

title: Portraits
context: The module ships generated silhouette portraits in brass frames as placeholders.
recommended: Keep the silhouettes until you have art; every portrait is one image you can swap on the actor.
alternatives: Use your own images now (tell me where they are)
No portraits; names only

title: Music
context: Foundry can play a playlist per scene. Nothing is bundled.
recommended: An empty playlist per location (Ashford, the Exchange, the Undercourses, the Gloam, the Binding House, the inn, the quay) for your own tracks.
alternatives: No playlists
Point me at a music folder to wire in

group: Found while building the system (10 Nov)
title: Does a Scene attempt cost an action?
context: Each approach in a Scene is attempted on a hero's turn.
recommended: 1 action per attempt, so a hero can try up to three times a turn (with no multiple-attempt penalty).
alternatives: 2 actions per attempt
1 action, with −4/−8 like Strike for repeated attempts

group: Found while building the system (10 Nov)
title: Critical failures on recovery checks
context: While Dying, a failed recovery check marks 1 of the 3 pips.
recommended: A critical failure (missing by 10, or a natural 1) marks 2 pips.
alternatives: Every failure marks 1 pip, critical or not

group: Found while building the system (10 Nov)
title: NPC checks and saves
context: The workbook gives benchmark enemies an attack bonus (5 + EL + grade compensation) but no separate skill or save numbers.
recommended: NPCs use their attack bonus for every check and save unless their sheet overrides it.
alternatives: Attack bonus − 2 for saves and checks outside their role
Set by hand on each NPC

group: Found while building the system (10 Nov)
title: Short rests for Unclassed heroes
context: Hit dice = Combat EL, so Unclassed heroes (EL 0) would have no hit dice to spend.
recommended: Everyone can spend at least 1 hit die on a short rest (d6 for the Unclassed).
alternatives: Unclassed heroes heal only on a long rest

group: Found while building the system (10 Nov)
title: Casting ability after binding
context: Spell DC and spell attack need a casting ability.
recommended: Set it to the class's primary ability when a hero is bound (CHA for Bloodcharged, INT for Theorist); you can change it on the sheet.
alternatives: Always choose it by hand at binding

group: Found while building the system (10 Nov)
title: Weapon and armour training after binding
context: Attack and AC add a proficiency bonus by training rank.
recommended: Binding makes the hero Trained in weapons and in the armour type their class suits; before binding everyone is Untrained.
alternatives: Trained in weapons from the start (professions teach tools)
Set by hand

group: Found while building the system (10 Nov)
title: Which skill a 'Craft effort' approach rolls
context: Some Scene approaches say 'Craft Effort' without naming a skill.
recommended: The hero's best Craft-track skill rolls the check.
alternatives: The approach names a skill each time
The hero picks any Craft-track skill and the GM rules on aptness

title: The Into the light Scene's numbers
context: Resistance 80, DC 12, 8 rounds of sun (one per step of the light on the map). In 2,000 simulated runs with the trio and a player character it was won 90% of the time, in about 5 rounds; Setbacks deal 1d2 and damage a loaner.
recommended: Keep these numbers.
alternatives: Harder: 6 rounds of sun
Easier: Resistance 60

title: Old Gnaw and the rats
context: Rat 4 HP, AC 11, +2, 1d3. Rat swarm 8 HP, AC 10, 1d4 to everyone Engaged. Old Gnaw 16 HP, AC 12, +4, 1d4+1, two bites and a Shove (DC 12). Simulated: the party wins 96% of the time and a hero drops in 44% of fights.
recommended: Keep these numbers (fair but tense, as you chose).
alternatives: Harder: Old Gnaw 22 HP
Easier: drop the swarm

title: Starting coin
context: Your character starts with 2 gold crowns 5 silver marks; each of the trio has 1 gold crown 5 silver. Loaners cost blade 5, lamp 6 and pry bar 4 gold (the 30 gp bill).
recommended: Keep these.
alternatives: Everyone starts with nothing but the pack
Your character starts richer (5 gold crowns)

title: The Coldwater sellswords
context: The module names them Harl Venn, Mags Orrin and Teague Pell, a crew called the Knotted Gull, with a mark of a gull over a knotted net (all Draft).
recommended: Keep as placeholders.
alternatives: Rename them (note)
Leave them nameless

title: Young Enkrid's flashback choices
context: Two Draft choices for young Enkrid during the prologue, plus the scruffy captain's closing line and the Scene's lose outcome ('come back at tomorrow's noon'), are Claude's.
recommended: Keep as Draft until you rewrite them in the journal.
alternatives: Remove the choices; the flashback is narration only

title: The trio's starting skills
context: Picked from each one's race, profession and class skills: Tova trains Athletics (instead of Survival twice), and all three are Trained in weapons once bound.
recommended: Keep these builds.
alternatives: Let me choose their skills on first import

title: The yes/no oracle's odds
context: d20, +4 when likely and −4 when unlikely, with bands at 3 / 7 / 10 / 13 / 17 for No, and / No / No, but / Yes, but / Yes / Yes, and.
recommended: Keep these odds.
alternatives: Use a 2d6 oracle instead
Only Yes / No, with no 'and/but'

title: The Act 1 milestone
context: At the end of Act 1 everyone's profession goes from Novice to Apprentice. Class stays at Novice (it was just bound).
recommended: Keep it.
alternatives: No milestone; XP only
Both tracks go up a rank

title: Shop and kit prices
context: Starting kits and the Ashford shop use F-grade prices (x3 per grade above F); the physician's tonic heals 1d6 + 1. The broker's board has eight Draft jobs; a rat cull pays 2 gold crowns.
recommended: Keep these prices.
alternatives: Cheaper, so coin matters less
Dearer, so the danger fee matters more
